source.title: Weight Standardization
source.authors: Siyuan Qiao; Huiyu Wang; Chenxi Liu; Wei Shen; A. Yuille

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no cutoff or garbling apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own normalization experiments, including training-error curves, but does not test the listed claim versions: it does not measure CIFAR training classification error, compare plain and shortcut networks, test the listed initialization or learning-rate conditions, or compare BN against the same network without BN for training speed.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses BN's training benefits and reports training-error curves for ResNet-50 on ImageNet under GN, GN+WS, and BCN+WS. The CIFAR tables report error rates but do not identify them as training error, so they are not rows for the claim. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: Figure 8 tests V6 in an additional setting: large-batch BCN is GN applied after BN (Eq. 43), so comparing GN+WS with BCN+WS adds BN while retaining GN and WS. The authors explicitly report faster reduction of training error. This does not test standalone BN against an entirely unnormalized network.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct: the authors argue that WS smooths optimization and alleviates elimination singularities, while BCN incorporates batch statistics and further improves training. Their broad performance conclusion should retain the reported video-recognition limitation: BCN improves GN but does not surpass BN there.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies weight and activation normalization in vision models, not the specified random-initialization, width, depth, or learning-rate tests.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different training dynamics across normalization choices (GN, GN+WS, and BCN+WS) and states that WS's centering component accounts for most of the observed training-speed improvement.

fits_no_version.finding: Weight centering supplies most of WS's training-speed improvement; weight scaling contributes slightly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ongoing weight standardization accelerates ImageNet ResNet-50 training with GN, principally through weight centering.

record.problems: The relevant training-error results are presented as figures without numerical endpoint values or uncertainty estimates in the supplied text. The reported classification tables primarily give evaluation error rates rather than training classification error.
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out. CIFAR tables report classification error rates without identifying them as training error; ImageNet validation error and other task metrics do not directly measure training classification error.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR training classification error, including random labels and dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Teacher-student spurious minima and extra student neurons.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth; WS acts throughout training.
Stability thresholds, curvature dynamics, catapult recovery, and divergence.
Higher learning-rate tolerance, standalone BN versus an otherwise unnormalized network, and Fixup's speed and stability without normalization.

record.verdict_notes: The record overlooks that large-batch BCN explicitly contains BN. Its controlled comparison with GN+WS bears on V6 even though most other comparisons concern the proposed methods' performance. Evaluation-error tables alone do not establish training speed or near-zero training error.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, random or corrupted labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and extra student width.
Plain versus shortcut networks across depth; the paper evaluates residual networks and does not compare them with plain networks.
The listed initialization methods and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training at and above stability-limit learning rates, curvature, sharpness, and divergence.
The paper does not compare BN against an otherwise identical network without BN for training speed or learning-rate tolerance, or test Fixup.
